proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof (identification of the limit), with the Jacobian kept abstract. In the parent, T = DF(b) and j = J(b) = normDet(DF(b)). The hypothesis there is LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume with finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n.
Notation: λ := volume on ℝ^n, H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^P.
1. The carrier of the submodule LinearMap.range T is the set range T = T(ℝ^n) (LinearMap.range_coe; simp).
2. Measure identity: H^n⌞range T = ofReal(j)·T_#λ. T is continuous, hence Borel. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel.
- (H^n⌞range T)(U) = H^n(U ∩ range T) (Measure.restrict_apply).
- U ∩ range T = T(T^{-1}(U)) (image_preimage_eq_inter_range).
- The hypothesis with S := T^{-1}(U) gives H^n(T(T^{-1}(U))) = ofReal(j)·λ(T^{-1}(U)), which equals ofReal(j)·(T_#λ)(U) (Measure.map_apply).
- Measures agreeing on Borel sets are equal (Measure.ext).
3. Integration.
- ∫_{range T} f dH^n = ∫ f d(ofReal(j)·T_#λ) = (ofReal j).toReal·∫ f d(T_#λ) (integral_smul_measure).
- integral_map applies because T is measurable and f is continuous, hence strongly measurable. It gives ∫ f d(T_#λ) = ∫ f(Tc) dλ(c).
- Since j ≥ 0, toReal(ofReal j) = j. So ∫_{range T} f dH^n = j·∫ f(Tc) dλ(c).
No integrability is needed in either identity. Injectivity of T is not needed either; in the application T is injective.
key_steps: The range submodule's carrier is Set.range T.
On Borel U, H^n(U ∩ range T) = H^n(T(T^{-1}U)) = ofReal(j)·λ(T^{-1}U), so H^n⌞range T = ofReal(j)·T_#λ.
integral_smul_measure and integral_map give j·∫ f∘T dλ.
